newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan March trade surplus seen down yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan March trade surplus seen down yr/yr.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus is expected to fall in March from a year earlier, with economists' predictions of the fall ranging from 1.5 percent to 17 percent.
Only one institution predicted a rise in the surplus -- Nomura Research seeing a slight expansion on expectations of a jump in exports in the last 10 days of the month.
In value terms, forecasts of the surplus ranged from 929 billion yen to 1.17 trillion yen, compared with a 1.12 trillion yen surplus in March last year.
The data will be released at 8.50 a.m. on Thursday (2350 GMT Wednesday).

Most economists said the March surplus would slip due in part to a healthy surplus the year before and in part as a result of higher imports brought in to feed stepped up manufacturing output as demand grew ahead of a rise in the consumption tax on April 1.
The sales tax was raised to five percent from three percent.
But economists also said it may be the last fall for several months as the year-on-year trend in the surplus is set to switch from a falling one to a rising one in April.

"Everybody agrees that it is rising, it is just a question of how fast," said Richard Jerram at ING Barings, adding that the surplus in seasonally adjusted month-on-month terms had bottomed out in April last year.

A Reuters quarterly poll of forecasts for Japan's trade balance showed the surplus is expected to expand to 10.5 trillion yen in fiscal 1997/98, compared with an expected surplus of around 6.6 trillion yen in fiscal 1996/97.

Despite recent comments by U.S. policy-makers warning Japan to avoid dramatic rises in the surplus, most economists said further pressure was unlikely in the short-term given strong U.S. economic growth and that a strong dollar was working to keep inflation low by keeping import prices down.
In February there was a seasonally adjusted month-on-month surplus of 462.03 billion yen.
